Claimed for dispatch as the **sixth** of the seven Ruling-A remediation cards. Card face declared: `packages/spec/src/system/metrics.zod.ts` plus its ADR-0087 migration entries, its generated artifacts, and its test file. Disjoint from #17782 (`system/logging.zod.ts`, in flight) on every authored source file; the two share only generated artifacts (`migrations/registry.ts`, `authorable-*/system.json`), which are regenerated, never hand-merged, and serialise **landing**, not claiming.

### Clause ② — `yes`

Recorded here at claim time, both carriers hung in the same write (`needs:contract-review` on this card; the PR side is owed the moment the PR exists). Mechanical floor, `references/contract-review.md`: **a new key on a published payload is always `yes`** — each rename puts a spelling on `MetricDefinition`, `MetricExportConfig`, `MetricsConfig` and `ServiceLevelObjective` that no author could write before. This overrides Ruling A's own `Clause-②: no`, exactly as corrected for the five sibling cards (recorded on #17784 `5652094166` and on #15939 `5652120294`).

### Staleness check — three faces, on `origin/main` @ `fc28c1d38`, 2026-09-13T10:38Z

| face | reading |
|:--|:--|
| action | `git log -20 -- packages/spec/src/system/metrics.zod.ts` → **one** commit (`2d34f320d`, #17846, rule-array `filter` doors). Nothing has renamed a duration key on this file. |
| card-reference | #15939 OPEN · PR #17635 OPEN (lands last) · #15678, #15679 both landed |
| work-item | all five keys still declared in key position and still bare: `maxAge` 1 · `interval` 1 · `collectionInterval` 1 · `window` 3 · `period` 2. Already-suffixed spellings (`*Ms`/`*Sec`/`*Seconds`/`*S`) on this file: **0**. Lit control `z.number` 38, dark control `zzqqxx` 0. |

⇒ premise holds; all five rows are still owed.

### The multiple-declaration hazard is real on this card

The card warns that line numbers rot and that keys here are declared more than once. Measured: **three of the five names have same-named decoys on this same file**, and each decoy is a `z.object({`, not a duration number.

| row | enclosing symbol path | shape | decoys on this file that must NOT move |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `:191 maxAge` | `MetricDefinitionSchema.summary.maxAge` | nested, `default(600)` | — |
| `:552 window` | `ServiceLevelObjectiveSchema.errorBudget.burnRateWindows[].window` | nested **inside an array element**, no default | `:346` `MetricAggregationConfigSchema.window` and `:442` `ServiceLevelIndicatorSchema.window`, both `z.object({` |
| `:623 interval` | `MetricExportConfigSchema.interval` | **top level**, `default(60)` | — |
| `:709 collectionInterval` | `MetricsConfigSchema.collectionInterval` | **top level**, `default(15)` | — |
| `:718 period` | `MetricsConfigSchema.retention.period` | nested, `default(604800)` | `:509` `ServiceLevelObjectiveSchema.period`, a `z.object({` |

The dispatch order carries this table and requires the row to be re-located by symbol path, with the decoy count re-measured, before any edit.

The full dispatch order follows in the next comment.

## Dispatch order — #17783

Epic PM for #15939 · `session_015c5G6TmpMKgnusmTpD7Ntt` · 2026-09-13T10:42Z · `mode:subagent` · base `origin/main` @ `fc28c1d38`

## Zone 1 — Adjudicated. Not reopenable by you.

Director seat on #15939, 2026-09-11T14:08Z, maintainer 「同意」, decision batch #115 — quoted verbatim, not translated:

> **Ruling A.** Batch #65's direction stands (the gate refuses a duration key whose JSDoc names a unit its describe does not). Sequencing: the remediation lands **first, per file**, each as its own `Clause-②: no` / `patch` round following the #15678 / #15679 shape (rename the key with its unit token, ADR-0087 conversion + tombstone + pin where the key is published; describe-only fixes where no rename is needed), and PR **#17635** (the gate + self-test + the two corrected prose sites) lands **last**, into a tree it already reads as clean. ⛔ Not B (18 published-key renames in one PR); ⛔ C is gate weakening.

Settled, ⛔ do not re-litigate any of these:

1. **Direction.** The five keys get renamed to carry their unit. "Should we instead fix the describe" is answered: no.
2. **`Clause-②: yes`, not the ruling's `no`.** Corrected by the epic PM before dispatch, recorded on #17784 (`5652094166`) and #15939 (`5652120294`). Mechanical floor: a new key on a published payload is always `yes`. Put `Clause-②: yes` in the PR body.
3. **`minor`, not the ruling's `patch`.** Every one of the #15678 / #15679 siblings shipped `feat(spec)!` at **minor** (`packages/spec/CHANGELOG.md` under `## 17.4.0`). The launch window refuses `major` (`scripts/pm/check-changeset-no-major.mjs`): breaking-ness is carried by a `**BREAKING**` banner plus the `adr-0087: registered` disposition, **not by the level**. Measure the sibling entries yourself and match them.
4. **Both ADR-0087 registrations, per key.** A D3 semantic entry **and** a `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` row. Settled for the whole epic on #15939. The two older tenant renames that carry only a semantic entry are residue of the pre-#4659 leaf-matching bug — ⛔ not a precedent.
5. **PR #17635 lands last.** ⛔ Do not touch `packages/spec/scripts/check-duration-unit-keys.ts` or its self-test. It is red by construction until every remediation card lands. That is designed, not a defect.
6. **Sibling files are not yours.** ⛔ `kernel/plugin-lifecycle-advanced.zod.ts`, `kernel/plugin-security-advanced.zod.ts`, `system/tenant.zod.ts`, `system/logging.zod.ts`, `system/tracing.zod.ts`. Five of the seven cards are delivered or in flight; two of them are already merged into `main`.

---

## Zone 2 — Mechanism assumptions. Falsify each before you rely on it.

Every line below is something I measured and could still be wrong about. Your first job on each is to re-measure. A measured contradiction is a good deliverable — report it, don't route around it.

### 2.1 The five rows, by symbol path — and the three decoys

Line numbers come from PR #17635's enumeration and **rot**. Re-locate by symbol path. Measured on `origin/main` @ `fc28c1d38`, 2026-09-13T10:38Z:

| row | symbol path | shape | JSDoc, as read | value |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `:191` | `MetricDefinitionSchema.summary.maxAge` | nested | "Max age of observations **in seconds**" | `int().positive().optional().default(600)` |
| `:552` | `ServiceLevelObjectiveSchema.errorBudget.burnRateWindows[].window` | nested, **inside an array element** | "Window size **in seconds**" | `int().positive().describe('Window size')`, no default |
| `:623` | `MetricExportConfigSchema.interval` | **top level** | "Export interval **in seconds**" | `int().positive().optional().default(60)` |
| `:709` | `MetricsConfigSchema.collectionInterval` | **top level** | "Collection interval **in seconds**" | `int().positive().optional().default(15)` |
| `:718` | `MetricsConfigSchema.retention.period` | nested | "Retention period **in seconds**" | `int().positive().optional().default(604800)` (`// 7 days`) |

⚠️ **Three of the five names have same-named decoys on this same file, and every decoy is a `z.object({`, not a duration number.** These must not move:

- `:346` `MetricAggregationConfigSchema.window` — `z.object({`
- `:442` `ServiceLevelIndicatorSchema.window` — `z.object({`
- `:509` `ServiceLevelObjectiveSchema.period` — `z.object({`

Re-measure the decoy counts (`window` 3 key-position declarations, `period` 2) and state them in the PR body. `grep -c` counts LINES — use `grep -o … | wc -l` when you mean occurrences. Give a lit control (`z.number` reads 38 on this file) and a dark control.

Read each JSDoc yourself. ⛔ Do not infer the unit from the default's magnitude — `default(60)` is consistent with 60 seconds and 60 milliseconds, and `interval` on the sibling card had a describe that named the wrong unit outright.

### 2.2 The suffix is `Seconds`, not `Ms` — and this file already decided that

**This is the first card in the epic whose rows are seconds.** The four before it were all milliseconds. ⛔ Do not carry `Ms` over by habit.

`#15679` already renamed a key on **this same file**: `ServiceLevelObjectiveSchema.period.duration → durationSeconds`, with its tombstone const `SLO_PERIOD_DURATION_RETIRED` still in place at `:521-528`. That is the nearest precedent there is.

Derive the spelling from the tree, not from me: count key-position `*Seconds`, `*Sec`, `*S` and any other second-carrying suffix across `packages/spec/src/**/*.zod.ts`, and count the competing spellings for each of the five stems (`maxAge`, `window`, `interval`, `collectionInterval`, `period`). Put the counts in the PR body. Two of them need a judgement call you must show your work on:

- **`maxAge`** — "age in seconds" reads awkwardly as `maxAgeSeconds`; check whether an `*AgeSeconds` or `*Age*` family already exists.
- **`period`** — `retention.period` is already inside a `retention` object; check whether the surface spells this `retentionPeriodSeconds`, `periodSeconds`, or something else elsewhere.

If a stem has no attested family spelling either way, say so and take the plain suffix, as the sibling card did for `debounceDelayMs`.

### 2.3 The ratchet moves for **two** of the five, and that split is the trap

`authorable-surface/*.json` records **top-level keys per def**. Measured from the generator/checker source, not assumed:

- `MetricExportConfigSchema.interval` and `MetricsConfigSchema.collectionInterval` are **top level** ⇒ the ledger **must** move: `[RETIRED]` markers beside the new suffixed rows, plus the matching `authorable-defaults` moves.
- `summary.maxAge`, `burnRateWindows[].window` and `retention.period` are **nested** ⇒ the ledger must **not** move.

Both readings are already attested by landed siblings: PR #17954's key was nested and correctly moved nothing; PR #17986's three keys were top level and correctly moved the ledger. **Same rule, opposite readings, both right.** Verify the granularity from `packages/spec/scripts/build-schemas.ts` yourself and state which of your five rows moves the ledger and which does not, with the reason.

⛔ Regenerate with `gen:schema`. ⛔ Never hand-edit a generated artifact. ⛔ Never add a baseline entry to a ratchet to make a check pass — that is maintainer-only and a red line.

### 2.4 `burnRateWindows[].window` is a shape no card in this epic has hit yet

It is a key inside **an array of objects**. Two things need deciding and neither should be invented silently:

1. Does `retiredKey()` on an array-element object behave the way it does on a plain nested object? Prove it with a test, not an assumption.
2. What path notation does the `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` row take for a key under an array? Look at how existing rows spell nested paths (`kernel/RuntimeConfig:resourceLimits.timeout` is the shape from PR #17983) and whether any existing row crosses an array. If none does, say so, pick the spelling that the checker actually reads, and **flag it in `open_questions`** for the contract review.

Related known limitation, for your awareness only: **#17969** records that `build-schemas.ts` check (b2) cannot verify nested `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR` rows the way it verifies top-level ones. Three of your five rows are nested. This does not block you and ⛔ is not yours to fix — but it means a green check is weaker evidence here than it looks, so lean on your own tests.

### 2.5 Tombstones, and the TDZ ordering trap this file will spring

Check `.strict()` on each enclosing object. Where it is absent, a bare deletion is an **ADR-0049 silent strip** — the value vanishes and the consumer gets a default where an operator set a real number. Every one of your five needs a `retiredKey()` tombstone whose message carries the FROM → TO mapping.

⚠️ `gen:schema` and `check:authorable-surface` both run with `OS_EAGER_SCHEMAS=1`, which makes `lazySchema` evaluate its factory at module load. **A tombstone string const declared after the schema that reads it is a temporal-dead-zone read.** PR #17983 hit exactly this and had to move its const above the schema. This file has five schemas and an existing const (`SLO_PERIOD_DURATION_RETIRED`) — check where each of your new consts has to sit.

### 2.6 Consumer packages — named, and each owes a real reading

This is a `domain:spec` lane requirement, not a suggestion: **a sweep inside `packages/spec` cannot see a consumer's fixture asserting the old spelling.** Run and report an exit code for each of:

| package | why it is on this list |
|:--|:--|
| `@objectstack/observability` | the metrics-domain package; 109 `@objectstack/spec` imports. Highest fixture risk on this card. |
| `@objectstack/core` | the runtime that consumed the sibling card's keys |
| `@objectstack/verify` · `@objectstack/cli` | schema-driven fixtures |
| `@objectstack/rest` · `@objectstack/qa` | published-surface fixtures |

My own measurement, which you should try to falsify: outside `packages/spec`, the six metrics defs occur 5 · 4 · 8 · 6 · 6 · 7 times and **every hit is prose** — the only files are `content/docs/references/index.mdx` and `content/docs/references/system/metrics.mdx`, both generated. `collectionInterval` outside `packages/spec`: **1**. `packages/observability` reads none of the six defs (0), on a corpus where `@objectstack/spec` reads 109. If that is right, this card has **zero in-repo code consumers** and the runtime leg is empty — but you must confirm it, because a wrong zero here is exactly the failure this list exists to catch. Report per-package exit codes either way; if you skip one, say which and why.

### 2.7 Pinned objectui

`git grep` the pinned checkout at `.objectui-sha`, re-read from this tree. Report every export of `metrics.zod.ts` and each of the five key names, with lit controls on that same corpus and a dark control. Zero without controls is not a reading.

⚠️ **The pin-citation lesson, twice-learned in this epic:** the citation must land on ONE source line. Sibling cards spent a cycle each on a citation split across a TypeScript string concatenation, which put `.objectui-sha` and the sha on different lines and made the checker miss it.

---

## Zone 3 — Suggested route. Deviate freely with evidence.

1. Worktree off `origin/main` @ `fc28c1d38`. ⛔ Never edit the shared checkout, ⛔ never `git stash`.
2. Re-locate all five rows by symbol path; re-measure the decoys; read all five JSDocs.
3. Settle the suffix per stem from tree counts.
4. Rename + `retiredKey()` tombstone per row, consts placed above their readers.
5. Fix each `.describe()` to name the unit — the describe is what the reference page renders and what an AI author reads.
6. Five D3 semantic entries (or one entry covering the file, if that matches how the siblings did it — check) **and** five `RETIRED_KEYS_BY_MAJOR[18]` rows. Regenerate `registry.ts` with `gen:migration-registry`; ⛔ never hand-merge it.
7. Regenerate every artifact: `gen:schema`, `gen:docs`. `check:generated` must read all artifacts current.
8. Tests: for each row, a refusal pin (the issue is **not** `unrecognized_keys`, and the message carries FROM → TO), an acceptance pin at the same magnitude with the same default, and a describe pin asserting the unit is published. Where an existing pin asserts a key stays bare — **this card is the sweep that pin was written to catch** — replace it, move it out of any `describe()` block whose header would become false, and record in its comment what it used to pin and why. ⛔ Never delete, `.skip`, weaken, or "fix green" a pin.
9. **Reverse-verify at least the two hardest new pins** by ablation: delete the tombstone line, prove the deletion on disk (anchor count and blob hash), re-run and show the expected tests red, restore under an `EXIT INT TERM` trap, and prove byte-identity (`git hash-object`, empty `git diff HEAD`, empty `git status --porcelain`).
10. `minor` changeset for `@objectstack/spec` with the `**BREAKING**` banner, the FROM → TO mapping for all five, and `adr-0087: registered`.
11. Merge `main` with **`bash scripts/pm/os-regen-merge.sh`**, never by hand. ⚠️ Its header records the trap: os-regen paths merge with exit 0 and zero conflict markers **while silently dropping one side's changes**. After the merge, assert the sibling migration entries are still present by exact-name grep with a dark control, and re-run `check:generated`.
12. Full gate sweep: `dispatch-gates --commands`, reconciled against `--ran … :: exit N`. Report derived / run / NOT-MEASURED / UNRUN and every non-zero exit with its classification.

### Known noise you should recognise rather than chase

- **`check-widening-tells` T1 on `retiredKey()` lines** is the known inverted false positive **#17955** — the lines it fires on make the accept set strictly narrower. ⛔ Do not reshape the diff and ⛔ do not weaken the checker. Record it.
- **Docs Drift Check will over-name pages.** Its anchor is a bare string literal from your new retirement constants; with `interval`/`period`/`window` as stems, expect a wide false-positive list. Check each named page for an actual metrics-config mention before you touch it, and record the finding — the last card in this epic will trip the same anchor.
- **`check:doc-authoring`** refuses tracker ids inside runtime strings. If you add any runtime prose, put the anchor in an adjacent `//` comment. ⛔ Never add a baseline entry.

---

## Deliverable and red lines

- **Draft PR**, `Fixes #17783`, `Clause-②: yes` in the body. ⛔ Do not turn it ready. ⛔ Do not enqueue. ⛔ Do not enable auto-merge. ⛔ Do not merge. The in-seat clause-② contract review at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` is owed first and landing is the PM's step.
- Hang `needs:contract-review` on the PR the moment it exists (the card side is already hung).
- ⛔ Never edit anything under `content/docs/releases/` — release-owned.
- ⛔ Never weaken a gate, lower a threshold, delete a required check, raise a ratchet ceiling, or skip a test.
- Capture every exit code **before any pipe** (`cmd > log 2>&1; ex=$?`). Route heavy runs through `scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh` and read the verdict from its own `VERDICT command-exit` line.
- Report as `os-dev-report` on this card: every reading with its command, its exit code and a UTC timestamp; an `open_questions` list for anything you had to judge (the array-path notation in 2.4 belongs there); and anything you measured that contradicts this order.

**A measured "the premise is false, here is the evidence" is a good outcome, not a failure.** Stop and report rather than inventing scope.

### Correction to the dispatch order, Zone 2.2 — sent to the dev 2026-09-13T10:46Z

Recorded here because a correction that lives only in the dispatch channel is a half state.

Zone 2.2 told the dev to derive the suffix from tree counts. That still holds, but **counting alone will get at least one of these five rows wrong**, because the counts cannot see a reasoned convention this file already carries. Two #15679 tombstone prose files, both about `packages/spec/src/system/metrics.zod.ts`:

| file | what it records |
|:--|:--|
| `migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.system__MetricAggregationConfig__window.size.ts` | `window.size` → **`durationSeconds`**, explicitly NOT the gate's mechanical `sizeSeconds` ("`size` is byte/row-count vocabulary everywhere else in this spec"). `windowSeconds` was **also** rejected — the parent key is already `window`, so it would read `window.windowSeconds`. |
| `migrations/entries/retired-keys/18.system__ServiceLevelObjective__period.duration.ts` | `period.duration` → **`durationSeconds`**, and it is "why the two `window.size` keys above land on `durationSeconds` rather than `sizeSeconds`: the file already spelled a window length as a `duration` one schema down, so the three measurements now read alike". |

Both cite one shared semantic entry, `system-metrics-window-durations-unit-in-key`.

⇒ this file has a **stated naming convention already in force**: on `metrics.zod.ts` a window length is spelled as a `duration`, and three measurements were deliberately made to read alike. Row `:552` (`ServiceLevelObjectiveSchema.errorBudget.burnRateWindows[].window`) is a **fourth window length in seconds on the same file** — the mechanical answer is `windowSeconds`; the file's own recorded convention appears to prescribe `burnRateWindows[].durationSeconds`, which does not stutter because the array name already carries "window". The same hazard applies to `maxAge` and `retention.period`, where `maxAgeSeconds` and `periodSeconds` are the mechanical answers and mechanical was already wrong twice on this file.

⛔ Not decided here. The dev decides and must **show the argument in the PR body the way #15679 showed its own**, including why the rejected spelling was rejected.

Two consequences recorded with it:

- The dev must check whether these rows belong under the existing `system-metrics-window-durations-unit-in-key` entry or under a **new sibling** entry. ⛔ #15679's entry is not to be amended — the rule PR #17983 established for #15678's entry is that a predecessor's scoped past-tense record stays true and the successor writes its own opening with how it relates.
- The two `window` decoys are now explained rather than merely flagged: `:346` and `:442` are `z.object({` whose inner `.size` has already been renamed to `durationSeconds` and tombstoned. ⛔ Neither is to be touched, and their `durationSeconds` is **not** evidence that any row of this card is already done.

I read that file, wrote the field from memory anyway, and did it twice on one card.

⇒ The correction above is the sanctioned instrument, ⛔ not a second `Claim:` (forbidden) and ⛔ not an edit of the posted comment (no such tool call exists here). The substance is unchanged: `yes`, on the mechanical floor that a new key on a published payload is always affirmative.

The same defect is present on **#17785**'s claim and is corrected there in the same way. I found it by running `--pair` on both open PRs rather than only the one I doubted — the discipline I recorded at `5652931475` after the first defect, which is what caught this one.
